findings.title: The compatibility boundary contradicts the real emit generations it claims to pin
findings.recommendation: A survey of every review emit on disk inverts the claimed model: ALL scorecard-generation emits (D3 cycle + this change's own) carry scorecard but NO spine kind and NO per-finding dimension; ALL pre-scorecard emits (B2→D1) DO carry kind. So (a) every real scorecard-generation emit fails the spine check with a confusing missing-field error instead of rendering — the historical-pass scenario is unsatisfiable for every pass that exists today; (b) 'emits without kind' as a PRE-scorecard marker is empirically inverted; (c) the mandated real 'pre-D3 no-kind' error fixture does not exist. Ripples: design.md's 'pre-D4 emits carry the required shapes' risk note (false); tasks.md 1.4.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Draw the render boundary at the D4 emit generation: full spine + scorecard + dimension-carrying findings render; everything earlier (incl. the D3-cycle scorecard/no-kind emits) fails with the clean pre-capability error; error fixtures pinned from the real D3-cycle and B2-era emits; rewrite the design risk note

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep scorecard-presence as the boundary but make it true: kind inferable from the filename prefix (not a validation failure) and the dimension-consistency check applies only when findings carry dimension; state both relaxations

findings.title: ADDED grammar contradicts an unmodified baseline SHALL in a file the change already modifies twice
findings.recommendation: The baseline '3-dimension scorecard reporting convention' mandates a Status column with brief metrics 'not just issue counts' whenever the scorecard renders as a table — the D2b/pinned review table is Dimension × severity counts exactly (and MUST be, per cell-rollup). Post-archive both mandates would stand. Add a THIRD orbit-conventions MODIFIED block scoping the Status-column scenario to verify/audit-style hand-rendered scorecards (or retiring it for review reports as superseded by orbit-report-rendering's grammar).

findings.title: Multi-line recommendation_options bodies have no specified rendered form
findings.recommendation: The grammar puts 'option bodies' under blockquote containment, but D2b — the goldens' sole source — renders options as the single line '- (<label>) <body>' with no contained variant, and nothing prohibits newlines in body. Pin the form in D2b (label line + >-contained body lines, matching the recommendation form) or normatively define option bodies single-line with the newline treatment specified and drop them from the containment list.

findings.title: D2b header rule contradicts the render-time-context requirement on iteration's source
findings.recommendation: D2b says 'internal = all five fields from the emit' — but Iteration is COMPUTED as the trail ordinal, never read from the record. Reword: 'internal = change/mode/reviewer class/depth from the emit; iteration = the same-mode trail ordinal (both genres)'.

findings.title: Residual prompt-centric vocabulary in the unmodified cascade requirement
findings.recommendation: 'Pushback discipline + decision-fork prompts handle ambiguous edits' — post-D4 ambiguity routes through the decision-lane protocol where the prompt is optional closure. Add a small sixth MODIFIED block rewording to 'the decision-lane protocol (per Disjunctive recommendation fields surface as decision forks)'.

findings.title: Impact bullet omits the finding_titles retirement
findings.recommendation: The bullet says findings_summary retired; the delta retires findings_summary AND finding_titles. Align.

findings.title: 'Enumerate the trail's pass artifacts' understates the resolution step
findings.recommendation: The genre-dispatch error requires enumerating ALL trail emits (to name a propose/apply genre cleanly); the ADDED scenario pins the right behavior — reword design/task to 'trail artifacts/emits'.

findings.title: Reader-tolerance sentence lacks the renderer carve-out
findings.recommendation: Add '(the report renderer's strict boundary is the named exception, per orbit-report-rendering)' so the cross-doc split is stated at the conventions source too.

iteration_note: Note: 0 of these findings appeared in prior runs. 8 new this run (trend: 16 → 12-ext → 7 → 0 → 9-ext → 8, CRITICALs 5 → 7 → 1 → 0 → 6 → 2). The pass's distinguishing move: an EMPIRICAL survey of every review emit on disk, which falsified the iter-2 boundary resolution's generation model — the newest emits lack kind/dimension while the OLDEST carry kind (spot-verified against this change's own emit and the B2 archive before persisting). The second CRITICAL is the un-delta'd Status-column SHALL in a file the change already modifies twice — class (a), sixth appearance.
commentary: The boundary CRITICAL is the best finding of the cadence: three passes reasoned about emit generations from the specs' own claims, and the first reviewer to actually open the archived files found the model inverted. It also explains itself — the spine's kind field was enforced by early conventions-era tooling and silently dropped from live practice around D2, exactly the kind of latent drift the D4 strictness surfaces. The choice it forces (option A's honest D4-generation boundary vs option B's inference-and-relax) is genuinely disjunctive: A gives cleaner determinism but renders nothing that exists today; B renders the D3 cycle at the cost of two relaxations in a strict validator.
